title: Accounting Basis for the Return of Carrier-Imposed Taxes on the Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
Where a ticket sold under the Air Ticket Fare Brands has fallen away unflown, the carrier-imposed taxes and fees the airline itself returns are paid back to the form of payment the traveller used, while the agency service fee is never paid back under this rule because the service it paid for has already been performed.

## 1. How the return is raised

A return of the carrier-imposed taxes on an unflown ticket is raised as a single line covering the whole booking, so that one movement settles every tax line the booking carries.

That return of taxes to the form of payment used stands alongside whatever the fare brand returns on its own terms, whether money or value on a voucher, because the taxes are the airline's to give back and the brand's terms reach only the fare.

## 2. The four quantities and the charge

2.1 **The taxes in question** are taken from the most recent tax line standing on the booking, multiplied by the travellers ticketed on it.
2.2 **The share returned** is the open share of that figure: 0.5 of it, which is to say 50 percent.
2.3 **The share in scope** is the whole of the trip's taxes: a share of 1.
2.4 **The insured share** is the whole as well, a share of 1, nothing being set against what a traveller's own protection cover has already met.
2.5 **The handling charge** kept from the sum returned is the standard charge of 25.00 USD.

## 3. How they assemble

The taxes in question, the share returned, the share in scope and the insured share are multiplied together in that order, and the handling charge is taken off the product of those four and never off any earlier step. The sum returned never falls below zero, and the result is rounded to the nearest cent.

## 4. Worked figure, on hypothetical inputs

A booking with 2 travellers ticketed whose most recent tax line stands at 86.40 USD.

| Step | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| the taxes in question: 86.40 USD taken for each of 2 travellers | 172.80 USD |
| multiplied by the share returned of 0.5 | 86.40 USD |
| multiplied by the share in scope of 1 | 86.40 USD |
| multiplied by the insured share of 1 | 86.40 USD |
| the handling charge of 25.00 USD taken off the product of those four | 61.40 USD |
| held at nothing were it lower, and rounded to the nearest cent | 61.40 USD |

Take the same booking with a most recent tax line of 18.00 USD instead. The taxes in question are 36.00 USD, the three shares leave 18.00 USD, and the handling charge of 25.00 USD would take the figure to less than nothing; the sum returned is therefore 0.00 USD.
